app.description: Scaffold a BeSpunky-standard app — the application sibling of publishable-lib. CREATES the app through the stack adapter (--stack; default: the workspace's own — Angular today, with the house defaults minimal/scss/routing/no-e2e), then ATTACHES every capability the workspace wears by running each active layer's per-app steps — the same steps a sync runs (the web dev loop's serve targets, the design system's sass channel + provider, the Firebase client, …). What the workspace wears is detected, plus --layers (what this run is bringing into being; house.sh passes its ensure set) and the legacy --firebase override. This is the single command for adding any further app to a BeSpunky workspace; never reach for the raw framework generator, which leaves the per-app config out.

serve-options.description: Set BeSpunky house dev-server options (host 0.0.0.0) on a project's dev-server target — the `dev-server` leaf created by the `serve` generator (legacy dev-server names tolerated for an upgrade). Strips any stray `host` off the composing `serve` target so it isn't forwarded as a flag.

serve.description: The Nx adapter of the house dev loop: a `dev-server` leaf (@angular/build:dev-server — host 0.0.0.0, configurations development (default) / production, buildTarget <app>:build — written only when the project has no dev-server of its own and is an Angular app) and the `serve` target (@bespunky/nx-tools:serve — a thin wrapper over the stack-free `tools/dev/dev serve <app>`), plus the app's entry in `.bespunky/dev.json` seeded from the adapters that apply (the dev-server process; the Firebase emulator suite in a Firebase workspace) — only what the app does not declare yet. Applied by the house `app` generator to every app and re-asserted by `house.sh upgrade`. Idempotent + self-healing (consolidates the raw @nx/angular `serve` into the `dev-server` leaf). The dev-only worktree tab label is the Angular adapter's: see `worktree-tab-label`.

dev.description: Write the stack-free dev engine and seed the dev declaration (the `web` layer). The engine — tools/dev/dev serve [app] [--worktree=<x>] [--port-offset=<n|auto>] [--skip=<id,…>] [--no-shared-browser] [--no-install] [--dry-run] — is generator-owned and Node-built-ins-only (no project node_modules): it reads `.bespunky/dev.json` (per app, processes {id, cmd, ports:{name:base}, env, primary, ready, url decorators, advice} + an install step), resolves ONE port offset for every declared port (the block sized from the declared ports; the main tree prefers the base ports, each worktree a stable verified-free block), substitutes ${PORT:name} / ${OFFSET} / ${TREE} / ${APP} and exports PORT_<NAME> / PORT_OFFSET, runs every process under one graceful Ctrl+C, registers `<slug>.localhost` and drives the shared co-driven browser to the app. Then seeds `.bespunky/dev.json` for every Nx project served by @bespunky/nx-tools:serve from the adapters that apply (Nx dev-server, Firebase emulators) — adding only process ids an app does not declare yet. A Python, Go or plain Vite project writes its declaration by hand and is served by the same engine. Workspace-level, no inputs; idempotent.

worktree-tab-label.description: The Angular adapter's dev-only worktree tab label: writes worktree-tab-label.ts into an Angular app and, when creating the capability (--wireProviders), wires provideWorktreeTabLabel() into its app.config.ts. On a `<slug>.localhost` worktree domain it prefixes the tab title with `[slug]` and tints the favicon by a hue hashed from the slug, so each worktree tab is distinct; tree-shaken from prod via ngDevMode. The `angular` layer's per-app step; the house `app` generator applies it to a new app.

devcontainer.description: Generate the BeSpunky-standard devcontainer, composed from the active layers: devcontainer.json, the image it builds (house.Dockerfile — the OS packages as one cached layer, through the installer house.packages.sh and the seeded os-packages.txt), one post-create.sh, and the persisted .claude, ~/.config and ~/.local.

claude-settings.description: Generate .claude/settings.json wiring the claude-toolkit + nx marketplaces (autoUpdate on) and enabling the active layers' Claude Code plugins.

gitignore.description: Keep what the active layers' tooling creates out of git: appends each layer's `.gitignore` block (Nx caches + the sync lock, node_modules, dist, .claude/data/, …) where not already mentioned, and tidies blank-line runs. The Nx floor's step — runs on every sync, with or without the agent layer. Idempotent.

angular-ai.description: Wire Angular's official AI tooling into the project. Writes project-scoped .mcp.json declaring the Angular CLI MCP server (`npx -y @angular/cli mcp`, always-latest) with its DEFAULT knowledge tools (get_best_practices, search_documentation, find_examples, ai_tutor, onpush_zoneless_migration); the experimental exec tools (build/devserver/test/e2e) are deliberately omitted because an integrated Nx workspace has no root angular.json and Nx owns those targets. Merges into any existing .mcp.json (preserves user-added servers). The Angular agent skills (angular-developer, angular-new-app) are NOT vendored here — post-create.sh fetches them fresh from github.com/angular/skills into .claude/skills/ on every container build; this generator just keeps that cache out of git.

firebase-emulators.description: The Firebase CORE, framework-neutral (needs only the Nx floor): firebase.json (emulator suite + functions source, singleProjectMode; never .firebaserc), apphosting.yaml (only with a client app — App Hosting serves a web app), the emulator/seed/secrets tooling under tools/, Cloud Functions as the `functions` Nx app (in the workspace's apps directory, or wherever it already lives), the workspace-level `firebase` emulator project, the .gitignore entries and the platform: ESLint firewall. --project=<app> additionally attaches the Firebase client to that app (via firebase-client), so one command still retrofits Firebase onto an app.

firebase-client.description: Attach the Firebase CLIENT to one app, through the app's stack adapter (Angular: environment files + per-env fileReplacements, firebase.config.ts and the per-service configs, emulator-overrides.ts, proxy.conf.mjs, provideAppFirebase(), firebase + @angular/fire) and tag it platform:web. An app whose stack has no Firebase port is reported, not crashed on. Composed by `app` in a Firebase workspace and by firebase-emulators --project.

playwright.description: Add @playwright/test — PINNED to the house Playwright version, never `latest` — as a devDependency of a JS project (the `js` layer), so its own browser tests have a runner and the devcontainer's post-create installs Chromium. Baseline only: an existing @playwright/test is never rewritten (moving a pin is a migration). The shared co-driven browser does not depend on it — it carries its own runtime.

shared-browser.description: Install the shared, co-driven browser tooling (the `web` layer). Writes the shared-browser CLI (tools/shared-browser/shared-browser, chmod +x), its Node/CDP helpers (attach.mjs, verify.mjs, recorder.mjs) and its OWN Playwright runtime (runtime.mjs — one pinned playwright-core + its Chromium, installed on demand into a per-user cache outside the repo, so it never resolves the workspace's node_modules and works in a Python or Go repo too; `shared-browser install [--with-deps]` provisions it ahead), and registers the workspace Nx project `shared-browser` with the lifecycle targets up|down|status|restart|clean|url|logs — thin wrappers over the bash CLI, which is the contract. ONE headed Chromium on a virtual display (TigerVNC Xvnc, resized to the viewer's tab), co-driven by a human over noVNC (a host port ALLOCATED per container from 6080-6119 through tools/port-claim — read the URL from `shared-browser url`) and by an agent over CDP (:9223, loopback). Workspace-level, no inputs; idempotent + upgrade-safe (every generator-owned file is rewritten on each run). The dev engine (tools/dev/dev serve, and `nx serve` through it) drives it per serve.

port-claim.description: Write tools/port-claim/ — host-port arbitration shared by every BeSpunky devcontainer on the machine (a claim file per port in a registry volume; atomic create-if-absent, ownership, expiry). The shared browser allocates its noVNC port through it; the worktree-domains proxy (:80) and the dev engine (an app's base port) ask it who owns a single-owner host port. Its own home, so no tool depends on a sibling's private file. Workspace-level (the `web` layer), no inputs; idempotent. `node --test tools/port-claim/` runs its suite, including a multi-process race.

worktree-domains.description: Install the workspace-level worktree-domains proxy + route registry (the sibling of shared-browser). Writes the CLI (tools/worktree-domains/worktree-domains, chmod +x) and its self-contained Node reverse proxy (proxy.mjs — Node built-ins only, no npm/apt dep), and registers the workspace Nx project `worktree-domains` with the housekeeping targets list|reconcile|status|logs|stop. One tiny proxy on 127.0.0.1:80 (loopback, container-internal, NOT forwarded) fronts every worktree's dev-server: a browser hitting http://<slug>.localhost/ (Chromium auto-resolves any *.localhost to loopback — no DNS/hosts) is routed by the leading DNS label to 127.0.0.1:<port> per the slug→port registry, and WebSocket upgrades are proxied so Angular/Vite HMR survives. The dev engine (tools/dev/dev serve, and `nx serve` through it) drives it per-serve via `worktree-domains register <slug> <port>` / `unregister <slug>` (idempotent; starts the proxy if down). Workspace-level and always-on — generated once per workspace for the `web` layer. Idempotent + upgrade-safe: every generator-owned file is rewritten on each run.

workspace-layout.description: DECLARE where this workspace keeps its projects: writes a named layout (`apps-libs` — apps/ + libs/; `packages` — packages/ for both) into nx.json `workspaceLayout`, Nx's own field, so the house generators and Nx's agree on where apps and libraries land. What `house.sh --layout=<id>` runs before the first project exists (an empty workspace has nothing to infer a layout from). A sync never runs it: an existing workspace's layout is DETECTED (nx.json, then where its projects already live). Moves nothing.

house-doc.description: Write the generated house docs — HOUSE.rules.md (the always-on directives, @-imported by CLAUDE.md so they are in context every session) and HOUSE.md (the mechanical how-to: serving, worktrees, Firebase, Nx, shared browser, Playwright, plus the toolkit version stamp) — and seed CLAUDE.md if absent before upserting a bounded, marker-delimited pointer into it. Moves the volatile house guidance OUT of the hand-owned CLAUDE.md (where an upgrade can't reach it and it went stale) into syncable docs. Workspace-level, always-on; idempotent (both docs fully rewritten; the pointer upserted between its markers, and the rest of CLAUDE.md left alone).

mark-extractable.description: Mark an existing Nx library as a reusable-tool extraction candidate: add the `reusable-tool:extraction-candidate` tag and write an extraction.json marker (proposed package name (default scope: the shared library workspace's, @bespunky), kind (the stack that owns the library), declared deps, and installed framework version ranges) so the host-side extract-tool can lift it into the shared workspace later. Sandbox-safe (touches only this workspace). PREREQUISITE: structure the generic code into its own clean Nx library first — this marks it, it doesn't abstract it.

adopt-extracted.description: Close the extraction loop: replace a local library (already published as @bespunky/<name>) with the public-npm package. Honours verify-then-delete — the default run adds the package + rewrites imports but keeps the lib; build to verify, then re-run with --finalize to remove the now-unused local lib. --keepShim instead leaves the lib as a thin re-export for staged migration.

navigation-core.description: Scaffold the self-contained navigation-core kernel as a real workspace LIBRARY (through the Angular adapter, tagged `type:navigation` — the navigation layer's detection key — in the workspace's libs dir) — the reusable base that domain-specific navigation builds on (the bespunky-engineering:typed-reactive-navigation pattern). VENDORS navigation-x verbatim (@bespunky/angular-zen/router-x/navigation): routeConfigFor / provideRouterX / useNavigationX / RouteComposer / strong Router typing (the auto-derived typed navigator). On top, BeSpunky reusable additions navigation-x doesn't yet ship: the BsNavLink directive that AUGMENTS Angular RouterLink via hostDirectives (inherits the real href + every RouterLink feature — queryParams/fragment/target/relative/RouterLinkActive — and adds only a typed composer binding + a `navigated` telemetry seam; it does not reimplement RouterLink), useNavigationLinks (the composer-value twin of useNavigationX, for binding links), RouteState (URL read-side signals), a typed EventBus + bindEvents, and navigation middleware. Files are copied byte-for-byte (no tokens, no formatting) to stay faithful to upstream; treat lib/* except extras/ as vendored. Adds @bespunky/typescript-utils (the kernel's type-util dependency). Run once per workspace: `nx g @bespunky/nx-tools:navigation-core [--directory=<lib dir>]` (default <libs-dir>/navigation-core); re-running rewrites the vendored kernel in the tagged library.

domain-navigation.description: Scaffold a domain's THIN navigation config — the per-domain layer of the bespunky-engineering:typed-reactive-navigation pattern, on top of the navigation-core kernel (run `nx g @bespunky/nx-tools:navigation-core` once first). Emits ONLY what is domain-specific: the typed route tree (routeConfigFor<Entity>().route(... as const)), the entity + event union + a domain EventBus<Event> subclass, the navigation file (useNavigationX/useNavigationLinks wrappers + the PURE event->navigator mapper + binding + provideX), and domain selectors extending RouteState. The composer, auto-derived navigator, the BsNavLink directive (real href so copy-link/open-in-new-tab survive), the event bus and the selectors base are INHERITED from navigation-core — never regenerated. The kernel import is pointed at the workspace's tagged navigation library (its package name or path alias). Run as `nx g @bespunky/nx-tools:domain-navigation <domain> [--directory=...]`; files land in <directory|<libs-dir>/<name>/src/lib>/navigation/.

publishable-lib.description: Scaffold a BeSpunky-standard publishable library through a STACK ADAPTER (--stack: `angular` → @nx/angular:library, ng-packagr FESM2022, standalone-only, prefix bs, Vitest (vitest-angular), modern nested ng-package.json with entryFile src/index.ts and NO umdModuleIds; `js` → @nx/js with bundler tsc, no ng-package.json). Default stack: the workspace's most specific. Lands in the workspace's libs dir under the workspace's own npm scope. Post-processes to the house standard: a per-project `nx release` block (version.currentVersionResolver git-tag + fallbackCurrentVersionResolver disk) and nx-release-publish.packageRoot dist/{projectRoot}. LINKING MODEL: in-repo resolution is the tsconfig.base.json PATH ALIAS the base generator writes — NOT package-manager workspaces (`workspace:*`) and NOT TS project references. Cross-lib deps (--workspaceDeps) are declared on the lib's own package.json as REAL caret ranges (`^<sibling's current version>`) and allowed through the stack's packager (Angular: ng-package.json `allowedNonPeerDependencies`). Test-only peers (vitest) are marked optional. --nonAngular is a deprecated alias of --stack=js. Never touches nx.json.

platform.description: Classify a project for the ESLint platform firewall: set its one `platform:` tag — `web` (browser/SSR; may depend on web + shared), `server` (Cloud Functions/Node; server + shared) or `shared` (isomorphic; shared only, no platform-bound package). `--platform` states it; without it the platform is INFERRED from the stack that builds the project, its imports of platform-bound packages (firebase-admin, firebase, the client framework) and the platforms of the workspace projects it imports — with the reason printed, and a refusal (with the evidence) when it mixes web and server. Written to project.json or the package.json `nx` block, whichever defines it. The command the firewall's lint guidance names: `nx g @bespunky/nx-tools:platform <project>`.

secondary-entrypoint.description: Add a secondary entry point to a publishable library: <lib-root>/<name>/{ng-package.json (entryFile src/index.ts), src/index.ts}, which ng-packagr auto-discovers by filesystem scan so it becomes the `<package>/<name>` deep-import subpath with no extra registration. In-repo, the deep import resolves through the tsconfig.base.json PATH ALIAS the delegated @nx/angular generator writes — that alias is the only in-repo resolution channel on the paths linking model, so it is deliberately KEPT. Generalized from xpand's design-system-secondary-entrypoint: delegates to @nx/angular's librarySecondaryEntryPointGenerator (skipModule), normalizes the nested ng-package.json, and RESETS the parent lib's tsconfig.lib.json include/exclude to a bounded, fixed-size glob pair (the delegated generator appends cumulatively, and N entries explode into a multi-MB tsconfig whose globs compile past V8's regex nesting limit — TS500 — killing the ng-packagr build). --component=standalone optionally scaffolds a standalone component and re-exports it; default --component=none leaves an empty src/index.ts the consumer fills. Standalone-only (no scam). For a DESIGN-SYSTEM component, use the `ds-component` generator, which composes this one and adds the sass channel + the house token-reading SCSS.

design-system.description: Create the workspace's DESIGN SYSTEM — the single source of visual truth every BeSpunky project is born with, because the alternative is that feature one typed a hex into a component, feature two copied it, and by screen five there is no system left to retrofit. Two halves: the framework-NEUTRAL core (tokens + SASS API) every design system gets, and a BINDING — the workspace stack's (Angular: composed through `publishable-lib --stack=angular`, a real publishable ng-packagr library with the `nx release` baseline and the tsconfig path alias), or else a plain source library carrying a DOM `setMode()` runtime. Lands in the workspace's libs dir, tagged `type:design-system`, with an import path from the WORKSPACE's scope, never @bespunky. An existing design system keeps the binding it was born with. Ships the MECHANISM and nothing else: design tokens as CSS CUSTOM PROPERTIES (the runtime layer — a theme change is a re-binding through the cascade: live, no rebuild, no second stylesheet), a ZERO-OUTPUT SASS API (the author-time layer: token accessors that @error on an unknown key, the one-and-only theme() emission, mixins, placeholders — with a PUBLIC barrel (`styles/_index.scss`, an explicit `@forward … show` contract) and the implementation in `_`-prefixed folders named for WHAT THEY ARE — `styles/_core/` (the token engine) and `styles/_utils/` (the authoring toolkit), never a folder called `internal`), the runtime half of the theming mechanism (Angular binding: DsTheme — the one thing that writes the `[data-ds-mode]` attribute, light/dark/system, SSR-safe — plus DsRuntimeTheme, which SWAPS themes at runtime — a theme being a standalone CSS FILE of token overrides authored in SASS via `ds.theme-overrides()` and generated by `ds-theme`, linked so it applies BEFORE first paint and keeping the compile-time unknown-token guard; JS token overrides exist only for values that don't exist until runtime, e.g. a colour picker), and STRUCTURE.md (where components and styles go when feature work produces them). It ships ZERO COMPONENTS and zero opinionated visual styles; token VALUES are loudly-marked PLACEHOLDERS that exist only so the library compiles and the app runs on day zero, and are replaced wholesale by the design phase (bespunky-product-ux:stage-the-vision -> realize-the-vision). Also opens the sass channel and installs the binding's provider on every app whose stack has a styles port (via design-system-styles). Workspace-level, always-on, idempotent: styles/ and src/ are SEEDED (written only if absent — an upgrade must never restore placeholder tokens over the project's real design); config, tags, docs and app wiring are re-asserted every run.

design-system-styles.description: Wire ONE app to the workspace's design system, through the app's stack adapter (its `styles` and `providers` ports; an app whose stack has none is reported, not crashed on). (1) The SASS CHANNEL: adds the design system's parent dir as a sass load path (Angular: the build's `stylePreprocessorOptions.includePaths`), so `@use 'design-system/styles' as ds;` resolves in-repo — necessary because the workspace links via tsconfig.base.json path aliases and SASS cannot read those, so a load path is the only channel; the specifier is deliberately the published one minus the npm scope. (2) CACHE CORRECTNESS: adds the design system to the app's `implicitDependencies`. The sass load path is not a graph edge on its own, so without an explicit dependency a token edit can leave `nx build <app>` replaying a CACHED bundle with the OLD tokens. This is deliberately an implicitDependencies edge (idiomatic; `nx affected` stays correct) — NOT a hand-rolled `inputs` array, which overrides the target's inferred inputs and hard-fails `nx build` on any workspace whose nx.json lacks the referenced named input (a real upgrade hazard). The step-4 provider import usually creates the edge anyway; this guarantees it. (3) The `@use` + `@include ds.theme();` marker blocks in the app's global stylesheet (two blocks, at opposite ends, because sass rejects a `@use` that follows any other rule). (4) the binding's provider (Angular: provideDesignSystem() in app.config.ts — only into an app of the binding's own stack), so DsTheme is instantiated at app boot (and writes the mode attribute from boot) rather than from whenever a component first injects it — for the default 'system' mode there is no flash to prevent (the CSS resolves the OS preference on its own); a persisted explicit choice still needs an inline <head> script to beat first paint. Self-detecting (finds the design system by its `type:design-system` tag) and a clean no-op when there is none. Composed by BOTH the `design-system` generator (for apps that already exist) and the `app` generator via the design-system layer's per-app step (so a LATER app is wired with no flag and no recollection that this workspace has a design system) — one code path, both directions. Idempotent and upgrade-safe: arrays merged and de-duplicated, stylesheet blocks upserted between their markers.

ds-theme.description: Add a THEME to the design system — a brand, a tenant palette, a user-selectable skin (`nx g @bespunky/nx-tools:ds-theme acme` -> packages/design-system/themes/acme.theme.scss, built to a standalone `theme-acme.css`). A theme is a CSS FILE of token overrides, NOT JavaScript, and that is the whole design: a `<link>` in <head> applies BEFORE first paint (a JS-applied theme lands after the bundle boots, so the user watches the default theme paint and then snap to the brand — a flash no service can fix); the browser caches and CDN-serves it for free; and because it is authored in SASS via `ds.theme-overrides()`, the design system's COMPILE-TIME guards survive — an unknown token name is a BUILD ERROR rather than a value that silently does nothing. Emits the same three-part structure the core theme does (`:root`, the per-mode blocks, AND the `prefers-color-scheme` blocks), so an override survives a mode switch and still applies for users on 'system' (the default — the most-missed case in hand-rolled theming). Registers the stylesheet on every app's build through its stack's `styles` port (Angular: `inject: false` + a `bundleName`, Angular's own mechanism for a compiled-but-not-auto-linked stylesheet), which is what makes it swappable rather than always-on. Swap at runtime via `inject(DsRuntimeTheme).use('theme-acme.css')`. Idempotent: the theme source is seeded and never overwritten; the build wiring is re-asserted. A theme can only RE-BIND declared tokens — it cannot introduce new ones.

ds-component.description: The Angular binding's component generator: promote a reusable component INTO an Angular design system, as its own SECONDARY ENTRY POINT (`nx g @bespunky/nx-tools:ds-component button` -> packages/design-system/button/, imported as `@<scope>/design-system/button`). One entry point per component — so each is independently tree-shakeable, is its own boundary, and no shared barrel becomes a merge-conflict hotspot. THIS IS THE ONLY WAY A COMPONENT ENTERS THE DESIGN SYSTEM: hand-creating the folder yields a component that resolves in the editor (through the path alias) and then VANISHES on publish, because the entry-point config IS the boundary. RUN IT ON THE SECOND OCCURRENCE of a UI pattern — the first card lives in the feature that needed it; the second time you do not copy it, you promote it, migrate BOTH sites, and delete the copies (two use-sites is exactly enough evidence to design the contract honestly; one is a guess, three is debt). Composes `secondary-entrypoint`, then adds the design-system specifics: the sass channel into the entry's own ng-package.json (so its SCSS can `@use` the token layer under ng-packagr), a starting SCSS in which every value is a TOKEN (making the right thing the easy thing at the exact moment a developer's first styling instinct lands), and an explicit public-API barrel (private members go in a `_`-prefixed folder named for what it holds — `_parts/`, `_material/` — and stay out of index.ts). Pairs with the bespunky-design-system:design-system-first skill, which carries the promotion discipline. A framework-neutral design system is refused with a clear message (it carries tokens and the SASS API only).

wiki-summary.description: Regenerate a library wiki's summary.json index (the compodoc `includes` SUMMARY). Devkit port of the legacy generate-wiki-summary Node script: walks the wiki folder via the Nx Tree (dry-run-safe, not raw fs), honoring per-folder .order files (split on /\r?\n/ — LF/CRLF-tolerant, fixing the old CRLF-only bug), building an ordered tree of { title, file, children? } where title = filename with dashes replaced by spaces and a folder gets children only when a sibling <folder>.md exists. Default wikiFolder packages/<lib>/wiki. Intended to also be wired as a Nx target in the docs build so summary.json regenerates in CI.

window-identity.description: Give the workspace a per-window VSCode IDENTITY so a project opened in one window is distinguishable at a glance from every other open window — an emoji in window.title (dock / Alt-Tab / window switcher) plus a quiet, design-system-coloured band on a bar (status by default; title bar or both optional). The deterministic WRITER of the feature; the bespunky-vscode-identity:window-identity skill is the intelligence that finds the design-system primary and a fitting emoji and passes them in. Colours are DERIVED, never hand-typed: from the design-system primary when one exists (--primary), else from a stable hash of the project name — so every project is distinct from birth, before it has a design system. Three properties make this a generator and not a hand-edit: (1) MERGE, never clobber — .vscode/settings.json is co-owned, so only the keys it owns (window.title + the identity colour keys) are re-asserted and the owned colour keys are cleared first so a surface change cleans up the bar it no longer paints, while every other setting the project added survives; (2) a no-clobber PROVENANCE RATCHET recorded in .vscode/.window-identity.json (name-hash < design-system < manual) so an upgrade's name-hash pass never downgrades a design-system or hand-picked colour, and an automated re-derive never stomps a human's manual choice; (3) DETERMINISM — colours are pure functions of (primary | name), so a sync regenerates byte-identical output. Committed team-wide by default; --personal git-ignores the settings + marker. Idempotent and upgrade-safe.
